one_liner_plain: Dexamethasone lowered 28-day mortality in hospitalized Covid-19 patients needing oxygen or ventilation

citation.title: Dexamethasone in Hospitalized Patients with Covid-19
citation.authors: RECOVERY Collaborative Group; Horby P, Lim WS, Emberson JR, et al.

sections.background: Covid-19 can cause diffuse lung damage, and much of the harm in severe disease seemed to come from the host's inflammatory response. Glucocorticoids might dampen that inflammation-mediated lung injury and so reduce progression to respiratory failure and death. But steroid evidence from related syndromes such as SARS, MERS, and severe influenza was weak, and there were real worries about delayed viral clearance. RECOVERY, a large pragmatic platform trial in U.K. hospitals, set out to answer the question quickly and at scale.

methods.design: Randomized, controlled, open-label adaptive platform trial comparing several possible Covid-19 treatments with usual care in U.K. hospitals. Patients were assigned in a 2:1 ratio to usual care alone or usual care plus dexamethasone.
methods.population: Hospitalized patients with clinically suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and no medical history that might put them at substantial risk if they took part. {{n:n_dex}} were assigned to dexamethasone and {{n:n_uc}} to usual care.
methods.intervention: Dexamethasone 6 mg once daily, by mouth or intravenously, for up to 10 days (or until discharge if sooner), plus usual care.
methods.primary_endpoint: All-cause mortality within 28 days after randomization.
methods.follow-up: 28 days, with outcomes collected at sites and through linkage with routine data sources.

sections.results: Mortality at 28 days was lower with dexamethasone: {{n:mort_dex}} versus {{n:mort_uc}} with usual care (age-adjusted rate ratio {{n:rr}}; 95% CI 0.75 to 0.93; P<0.001). The benefit depended on how sick patients were at randomization. Among patients on invasive mechanical ventilation, mortality was {{n:imv_dex}} versus {{n:imv_uc}} (rate ratio {{n:rr_imv}}). Among those on oxygen without invasive ventilation it was {{n:o2_dex}} versus {{n:o2_uc}} (rate ratio {{n:rr_o2}}). Patients on no respiratory support saw no benefit: {{n:none_dex}} versus {{n:none_uc}} (rate ratio {{n:rr_none}}), a result the authors describe as consistent with possible harm. Patients given dexamethasone also left hospital sooner (median {{n:stay_dex}} vs {{n:stay_uc}}), were more likely to be discharged alive within 28 days (rate ratio {{n:rr_dc}}), and were less likely to progress to invasive mechanical ventilation (risk ratio {{n:rr_prog}}).
sections.conclusions: In patients hospitalized with Covid-19, dexamethasone lowered 28-day mortality among those receiving invasive mechanical ventilation or oxygen alone at randomization, but not among those receiving no respiratory support. For ventilated patients the absolute reduction was 12.3 age-adjusted percentage points, about a one-third proportional reduction.
sections.limitations: The trial was open-label, although its primary outcome, death, is objective. Only essential data were collected, with no physiologic, laboratory, or virologic measures, so the mechanism of benefit cannot be studied here. This is the preliminary report of one comparison in a platform trial. Patients on no respiratory support saw no benefit, and the data are consistent with possible harm in that group.
sections.practice_impact: RECOVERY made dexamethasone the first drug shown to reduce Covid-19 deaths. The results were announced on June 16, 2020, and adopted into U.K. practice the same day. Low-dose dexamethasone for patients who need oxygen or ventilation became standard care worldwide, while steroids are avoided in hospitalized patients who need no respiratory support.

hero_findings.headline: 28-day mortality with dexamethasone (usual care: 25.7%); rate ratio 0.83
Mortality among ventilated patients with dexamethasone (usual care: 41.4%)
Mortality on oxygen only with dexamethasone (usual care: 26.2%)
No oxygen at randomization: no benefit (usual care: 14.0%; rate ratio 1.19)

must_include_map.excerpt: Overall, 482 patients (22.9%) in the dexamethasone group and 1110 patients (25.7%) in the usual care group died within 28 days after randomization (age-adjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.93; P<0.001).

In the dexamethasone group, the incidence of death was lower than that in the usual care group among patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (29.3% vs. 41.4%; rate ratio, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.81) and among those receiving oxygen without invasive mechanical ventilation (23.3% vs. 26.2%; rate ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.94)

In patients hospitalized with Covid-19, the use of dexamethasone resulted in lower 28-day mortality among those who were receiving either invasive mechanical ventilation or oxygen alone at randomization but not among those receiving no respiratory support.
